key_reasoning.reason: 8 production files across 4+ components and several subsystems: agent streaming callback (per-author error-streak and in-flight run-id tracking), LangGraph agent (truncation check per updates node, consecutive-tool-error abort), supervisor coordinator (handoff tracker reset on fatal error), core ThreadedGenerator (close(error, reason) + cancellation_reason contract), core exceptions (new MaxConsecutiveToolErrorsExceededException), config, plus assistant and hedged REST stream handlers. Shared foundations (core/thread.py, core/exceptions.py) are modified, which is why this lands at XL rather than L.

No exact precedent for converting a token-limit / context-overflow condition into a terminated run with a typed error. The change lives in the streaming/threading path: thought finalization ordering (the erroring tool's thought must be closed before the abort raises, CR-003), concurrent same-author tool calls vs sequential retries (CR-002), hedging cancellation reason plumbing, and OTel span-liveness ordering around stream.close(). Behaviour is gated by AI_AGENT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_TOOL_ERRORS, which keeps rollback tractable but does not remove the correctness risk. No security or persistence surface.

17 code files (8 production + 9 test) after excluding the 8 previous-slice SDLC doc artifacts committed on the shared branch. 17 crosses the 16+ XXL threshold by one file; the split is modification-heavy (few or no new files) and the 2437/69 diffstat is inflated by the doc artifacts, so this is the weakest of the high scores and sits right on the XL/XXL line.
